verdict: HSConfig is designed to keep arbitrary Wild deck generation load-safe and non-blocking, while exposing residual source and mechanic debt as diagnostics instead of blocking valid package generation.
evidence: tests/test_universal_wild_no_block_matrix.py asserts VALID_PACKAGE, load_safe_apply, runtime_apply_allowed=true, no hard block, and default_only_runtime_surfaces=[] across the representative Wild deck matrix.

The same matrix asserts source_to_runtime_explainability authority=diagnostic_only, apply_blocking=false, per-card closure rows, and closure lanes limited to runtime_backed, source_action_needed, diagnostic_only, or baseline_only_visible.
src/hsconfig/source_contract_audit.py maps unsupported or future claim kinds to diagnostic first_missing_link states rather than a runtime hard block.
docs/operator/README.md and docs/operator/guide-research-policy.md keep source-contract reports diagnostic and operator_summary.json as the normal apply authority.
risks: Representative tests cannot prove every possible future Wild deck or every future mechanic; they prove the no-block contract shape and known mechanic families.
A valid but source-thin deck can still be load-safe while not being strategically optimal; this is intentional for autonomy but must remain visible through diagnostics.
Unsupported future claim kinds may require new claim-kind policy rows before they can lower into runtime config.
recommended_actions: Keep arbitrary-deck unknowns non-blocking as long as the package is load-safe.
Add future mechanics by extending claim-kind policy and closure tests, not by adding ad-hoc runtime bypasses.
Preserve representative Wild matrix coverage and add focused decks only when a real deck exposes a concrete gap.
no_default_only_verdict: No silent default-only should be accepted. Current representative tests require default_only_runtime_surfaces=[] and mulligan_policy_status.default_only=false, while diagnostics expose any baseline-only risk.
slimness_verdict: The current design remains slim if it keeps one normal command path, one apply authority, and diagnostic reports as explainers only.
autonomy_verdict: Autonomy is best served by always producing a valid load-safe package when possible, using policy-backed mulligan and source diagnostics instead of human approval gates.
